title: Today in one sentence
text: Wall Street opens today after a rough Wednesday, when the S&P 500 fund SPY lost 1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ lost 2.0%; the big thing to watch at the open is how chip stocks react to TSMC's full earnings report.

title: Prices shown are Wednesday's close
text: The market has not opened yet, so every price on the board is still from Wednesday's close. Stocks fell that day after an inflation report showed prices rising a bit faster than experts expected. When prices rise faster, people worry that interest rates will stay high, and high rates tend to hurt stocks that already cost a lot compared with what they earn.

title: TSMC reports its full results today
text: TSMC makes chips for many AI companies. On Oct. 8 it said its July to September sales were a record, about 50% above a year earlier and above what analysts expected. Today it shares its profit and its plan for the coming months. We have not confirmed those numbers yet, so check TSMC's own report. Its outlook can move NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom and others on your list.

title: Some AI stocks are far below their highs
text: Rocket Lab is about 61% below its 52 week high, Vertiv about 41% and Broadcom about 30%, while NVIDIA is only 9% below and AMD 13%. A stock that fell a lot is not automatically cheap; it can mean the market sees more risk. AMD costs about 145 times its yearly profit, so it is the one most sensitive to interest rate worries.

title: The calm corners held up on Wednesday
text: Eli Lilly rose 3.8%, Lockheed Martin 3.6% and the dividend fund SCHD 1.0%, while most of the list fell. Healthcare and consumer staples (food and household goods) were the only big sectors that went up on the Nasdaq. This is why mixing different kinds of companies can make the ride smoother.

title: Lesson 8: Bonds vs stocks
text: A bond is a loan. You lend money to the government or a company, and they pay you interest and give the money back later. The 10 year US Treasury bond, a loan to the US government, paid an average of 4.99% in September, up from 4.06% a year earlier (see the chart on the board). When a very safe bond pays that much, stocks have to look attractive to compete, which is one reason expensive stocks wobble when yields rise. Stocks can grow more over many years but swing more; bonds usually swing less but grow less. Bonds are not risk free either: if rates rise, the price of an existing bond falls.

title: What this covers
text: Prices are from Wednesday's close because the market has not opened yet. Analyst price targets and company numbers are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, GE Aerospace and Lockheed Martin. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have prices and risk scores only. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell anything.
